articles.title: Man with Alzheimer's found alive after 11 days lost in jungle
articles.summary: Rescue workers said the man survived in the jungle by eating berries, drinking water from natural sources and making bedlike structures with the leaves of ac...
articles.body:
An elderly man with Alzheimer's disease who survived 11 days on his own in the Amazon rainforest is currently recovering at a hospital in the Brazilian city of Macapa, as rescue workers reveal more details about his surprising ordeal.

Janarino Ferreira dos Santos, 74, was rescued by park rangers and volunteers on Friday in a thick patch of rainforest about 6 miles from Macapa in northeastern Brazil. Rescue workers said Dos Santos was able to survive in the jungle by eating berries, drinking water from natural sources and making bedlike structures with the leaves of acai palms, where he could rest for the night.

"When he was younger he had worked in the rainforest, so he knew how to get around," said Aniel Cardoso, a park ranger who helped find dos Santos.

Cardoso and a group of volunteers who joined the search for dos Santos on Friday said they were able to find the man after they identified his footprints and realized he had been walking around in circles. As they tracked dos Santos' footprints, the rescuers came across a bed made from acai leaves that looked like it was at least four days old. Later, they came across a second bed with leaves that seemed to have been taken down from a palm tree that same morning.

"That's when we realized he could be alive, and that he could be close," Cardoso said. The rescuers found dos Santos in a thick patch of the forest, sitting down barefoot and wearing only underwear.

"He wasn't able to talk, he was no longer walking and he was very thirsty," Cardoso said.

The search, which started a day after the man went missing, brought together family members, volunteers and public safety teams, who faced difficult conditions in the forest. Firefighters and specialized teams used ground searches, helicopter and drone overflights as well as thermal cameras to look for signs of the missing man.

After nine days of searching and no news of dos Santos emerged, his granddaughter Sara Montes urged firefighters to keep looking for him. In a video posted on Instagram, she said they planned to suspend the search on Sunday, November 22.

"Don't forget about us. Don't forget about Grandpa," she pleaded.

Getting dos Santos out of the forest proved challenging as dense vegetation, flooded areas and swampy grounds prevented him from walking unaided, so rescuers improvised a stretcher using ropes and carried him through the difficult terrain.

A video posted on the G1 news site shows several men carrying him through the forest on the makeshift stretcher.

Cardoso said the man had walked out of his home on the edge of the rainforest while his relatives were visiting a neighbor.

He said that finding dos Santos was "very gratifying" because two months ago, another man had gone missing in the rainforest near Macapa, but had already died by the time he was found by rescue workers.

"This time, thank God, we were able to deliver this citizen alive," Cardoso said.

The dramatic rescue comes just over a week after a 17-year-old boy with autism was found alive after six days lost in eastern Australian woodlands.

articles.title: Deepam row: Members of Hindu outfits protest, clash with cops as lamp not lit at 'Deepathoon'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A scuffle broke out between members of Hindu outfits and Tamil Nadu Police on Tuesday at Thiruparankundram after the Karthigai Deepam was lit
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A scuffle broke out between members of Hindu outfits and Tamil Nadu Police on Tuesday at Thiruparankundram after the Karthigai Deepam was lit at the usual spot instead of the ‘Deepathoon’, despite the Supreme Court's order.Leaders of Hindu outfits and BJP staged a protest at the entrance to the hill pathway and raised slogans against the government.Officials tried to disperse the protesters and warned them of a lathi charge if they continued their demonstration.“The gathering you have assembled is an unlawful assembly. Disperse immediately, otherwise you will have to be dispersed by lathi charge,” read a placard displayed by the police.This comes after the ceremonial lamp was lit atop the Arulmigu Uchipillayar Temple in Thiruparankundram, instead of at the disputed stone pillar, or ‘Deepathoon’, atop Thiruparankundram hill, as directed by the Supreme Court.The ceremony was held amid heightened security, with police detaining several people citing apprehensions of disorder based on intelligence inputs and their past conduct.Also read |BJP says, officials deceived judges just like children are deceived with chocolatesSeveral BJP leaders and members of Hindu organisations were also detained across Tamil Nadu as police enforced restrictions ahead of the ceremony.Later in the day, the Madras high court's Madurai Bench, however, directed the Tamil Nadu government and all authorities concerned to comply with the Supreme Court's November 20 order permitting the ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon.It also directed officials to release all persons unlawfully detained under prohibitory orders imposed in Thiruparankundram.The direction was issued to the district collector, police commissioner and temple authorities amid restrictions surrounding the ceremonyAlso read | Congress hails Karthigai Deepam lighting at traditional spotThe dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thiruparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.The Subramaniya Swamy Temple is situated at the foothills, while a Dargah is located near the hilltop. A Shiva temple is also situated on the hill.Hindu groups maintain that the stone pillar where they seek to light the lamp belongs to the temple, citing civil court decisions dating back about a century.Dargah officials and Muslim organisations have opposed the proposed lighting, citing its proximity to their place of worship. The dispute involves questions of ownership and the rights of the respective parties.On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah.The apex court specified that the ceremony must be conducted by an authorised team and barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Calls for review into 'nightmare' Alderney air links
articles.summary: Alex Snowdon has written a letter calling for the review after more flight cancellations.
articles.body:
A politician has called for an urgent review into Alderney's air links after a number of flights were cancelled over the weekend.

Alderney States member Alex Snowdon has submitted a letter to Guernsey's Scrutiny Management Committee to raise his concerns, describing the current state of services as "a nightmare".

His comments follow ones raised by Steve Roberts, when he said the inconsistency of flights to and from the island could present a "very real" risk to life if hospital appointments were missed .

Aurigny said this weekend's cancellations were due to a mixture of technical and weather-related issues, but added services had "fallen well short of expectations in recent months".

Snowdon said that, while people accepted when there are cancellations caused by the weather, "this goes far beyond weather conditions".

He said: "There doesn't seem to be enough crew, and planes that are promised aren't being delivered - it's just a repeat, and repeat, and repeat."

Snowdon explained: "It's just got to such a state that no-one really has any confidence when they go to the airport whether they will be travelling or not.

"I think we need to find a way forward because this feels a bit like a nightmare."

Snowdon said he hoped there would now be some independent scrutiny of the services, which are operated by the Guernsey States-owned company Aurigny.

As part of the review, he said he wanted the scrutiny committee led by Deputy Andy Sloan to seek information from the States of Guernsey on details such as the contract between Aurigny and Skybus.

As part of that deal, the Isles of Scilly Steamship Company's Skybus airline is supposed to be providing Aurigny with two Twin Otter aircraft .

He added that he thought "it feels in the last six to 12 months that things have got considerably worse".

Deputy Andy Sloan confirmed the Scrutiny Management Committee would conduct a review of air links, and "the committee has been planning a review of the air route framework for the whole of the bailiwick for 2027".

He said: "So this request probably dovetails into that, and probably would bring forward a part of that review."

He added, however, it would likely not be reviewed until after Christmas.

Aurigny's chief commercial officer Philip Saunders has previously said: "Aurigny recognises the air services to and from Alderney, which are operated by Skybus, have fallen well short of expectations in recent months.

"We regret the disruption and take the responsibility to deliver the service with the utmost seriousness."

The BBC has asked the States of Guernsey to comment.

articles.body: MADURAI: Karthigai Deepam was lit at the traditional site above the Uchi Pillayar temple on Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai on Tuesday evening amid heightened security and continuing tension over the deepam-lighting controversy. But there was no sign of lighting of a lamp on the deepathoon.Tension prevailed at entry point to the hill in the evening when Hindu outfits members raised slogans against the Tamil Nadu govt. They thrashed a police vehicle and broke its windowpanes.The Supreme Court had permitted a restricted team authorised by the Madurai Subramanya Swamy Temple administration to light the lamp as a one-time arrangementThe lighting followed preparations at the site earlier in the day, when the copper cauldron, ghee, camphor and cotton cloth required for the ritual were taken uphill.More than 5,600 police personnel were deployed in the Thiruparankundram areas, including 1,163 personnel atop the hill, as authorities imposed restrictions on public access to the deepam-lighting site.Police restricted the movement of BJP leaders planning to visit Thiruparankundram. Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran was placed under house arrest in Tirunelveli, while former Union minister L Murugan was intercepted by police in Coimbatore district.The Tamil Nadu govt on Tuesday evening informed Madras high court that arrangements were being made to comply with the Supreme Court's direction to light deepam at the deepathoon.A division bench of Justice G R Swaminathan and Justice M D Sumathi issued a John Doe injunction restraining the public from calling to not implement the Supreme Court's direction to light Karthigai deepam at the deepathoon. The judges directed to release all people who were detained illegally."Article 144 mandates all authorities in the territory of India to act in aid of the Supreme Court. The district collector is a civilian authority and Article 144 will squarely apply to him since officials brazenly defied judicial authorities last year in connection with Karthigai Deepam event, we deem it fit to remind that collector is a public servant answerable only to Supreme Court and should ignore any contra advice given to him. Pendency of review petition is not a ground for not complying with the order," the judges observed.The judges observed that the prohibitory order issued should not come in the way of exercise of fundamental rights under Article 25 of the Constitution. The judge asked all authorities including collector, temple authorities to comply with the Supreme Court's directions.During the course of hearing, the state submitted that the prohibitory order had been issued only to prevent unauthorised persons climbing up the hill. There is no restriction to movement of devotees to the temple. articles.title: 'Population growth a strategic issue, can help repel enemy threats': Iran's Mojtaba Khamenei
articles.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Tuesday linked population growth to national strength, saying a larger young population would help the country
articles.body: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Tuesday linked population growth to national strength, saying a larger young population would help the country counter the "threats and malicious intentions of the enemy".His remarks came during Iran's Fourth National Event on Population Rejuvenation."This strategic issue that helps to shape the future, which our illustrious, martyred Leader had repeatedly emphasised over the past decades, is highly effective both in actualising the nation's capacities and in creating and enhancing many opportunities in science, culture, economics, and society," a statement quoted Mojtaba Khamenei as saying. He was referring to his father and predecessor, Ali Khamenei.The Iranian Supreme Leader further claimed that population growth is also influential in "repelling and removing the threats and malicious intentions of the enemy".Mojtaba's reference to the "enemy" appeared to be aimed at the United States and its ally Israel. Ali Khamenei was killed in a US-Israeli strike in Tehran on February 28, triggering a wider war in the Middle East.In his statement, Mojtaba, whose whereabouts remain unknown, also called for population growth to be treated as a "strategic national priority"."Giving serious, comprehensive attention to facilitating marriage at a young age, ensuring individual health, which depends on multiple factors, supporting childbearing, promoting a family-centred culture and highlighting successful examples in this area are all effective steps towards making Iran stronger," he said.He also stressed the need to communicate the importance of population growth to the public, particularly young people, and called for infrastructure supporting family welfare to be made a permanent part of national planning.Mojtaba further acknowledged shortcomings in previous population policies, emphasising that correcting them and pursuing a strategy focused on increasing the young population would be crucial to Iran's future."Without a doubt, every patriotic Iranian who hopes for a bright and glorious future for this land and its people will have a strong determination and resolve to ensure the continuity of future generations of the Iranian nation in a manner befitting the New Islamic Civilisation," he said."I sincerely hope that by remedying the shortcomings arising from certain past population policies and by earnestly pursuing the sound, strategic policy of increasing the young population and placing the family at the centre of this effort, our dear homeland will safely navigate this critical juncture and stage, which it now finds itself in and which will shape the future," he added.(With ANI inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: The OGs reunite: SAD gets 'bada bhai' tag in Punjab, but BJP has bigger ambitions
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Two of Punjab's oldest political allies are back together, six years after a bitter parting over the contentious farm laws.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Two of Punjab's oldest political allies are back together, six years after a bitter parting over the contentious farm laws. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, reviving a partnership that once governed the state for 15 years across three terms.The reunion, announced on the Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, brings together parties whose relationship was famously described by former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal as "nau-maas da rishta", the bond between the nail and the flesh.Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the development, saying the alliance would put Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first."Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," he said in a post on X, adding that the partnership, nurtured by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, LK Advani and Parkash Singh Badal, had "stood the test of time".Union home minister Amit Shah, who announced the reunion alongside BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, called the Akali Dal the NDA's "oldest ally" and said PM Modi had described the development by saying the "NDA is now complete".Shah also said SAD would retain its senior-partner status, adding that the "big brother" would get the chief minister's post. "Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats. Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," the Union minister said at the joint press conference.The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although the seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised.The reunion comes after months of political manoeuvring, including Sukhbir Badal's meeting with PM Modi in August and a shift in SAD's position on the Centre's delimitation proposal. It also brings together two parties whose electoral fortunes have declined sharply since their separation.However, Punjab is no longer the state in which the old alliance enjoyed its strongest run. AAP has emerged as the dominant force, Congress remains a significant contender, and the BJP and SAD have both undergone changes in their support bases and political strategies.Why SAD-BJP patched upThe partnership actually predates the BJP. Its predecessor, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, shared power with the Akalis in Punjab as far back as 1967 and 1969. The modern alliance, however, was forged in 1996, when SAD's Moga Declaration pivoted from purely Panthic politics to a broader pitch of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat."The partnership brought together the Akalis' predominantly rural Sikh support base and the BJP's largely urban Hindu constituency. It also helped both parties build a political coalition in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab.The alliance won 93 of 117 assembly seats in 1997, with SAD securing 75 and the BJP 18. After losing power to Congress in 2002, the combine returned to office in 2007 and retained power in 2012, winning 67 and 68 seats respectively.ALSO READ: From 'nau-mass da rishta' to bitter rivals and back; how BJP-SAD relations played out over the yearsBut the emergence of AAP, coupled with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, weakened the alliance. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three.The final rupture came in September 2020, when SAD walked out of the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws. Sukhbir Badal's wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister on September 17, and the Akali Dal formally ended its 24-year-old electoral partnership with the BJP nine days later.The laws were repealed in November 2021, but the political damage endured.The alliance's decline is evident from its electoral record. In 2007, SAD won 48 seats and the BJP 19, taking their combined tally to 67. They improved to 68 seats in 2012, with SAD winning 56 and the BJP 12. But the numbers fell sharply thereafter. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three. By the 2022 assembly elections, the two parties managed just five seats between them, with SAD winning three and the BJP two.In 2022, SAD secured 18.38% of the vote and the BJP 6.60%, while AAP swept the election with 92 seats and a 42.01% vote share.Their separate performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections provided another reason to reconsider the alliance. The BJP failed to win any of Punjab's 13 seats despite securing 18.56% of the vote. SAD won one seat, Bathinda, with 13.42%.ALSO READ: From 9.63% to 18.56% - BJP’s saving grace after drawing a blank in PunjabTogether, their vote shares added up to nearly 32%, compared with 26.30% for Congress and 26.02% for AAP.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The numbers make a case for pooling their support bases, although the combined vote share does not automatically translate into transferable votes or assembly seats.For the BJP, the alliance offers access to SAD's traditional rural and Sikh support networks. For the Akali Dal, it brings back a national ally and an opportunity to rebuild its electoral machinery, which is the BJP's strong suit.Sukhbir Singh Badal described the reunion as more than an electoral arrangement."This is not just a political alliance. There is an emotional bond. As my late father used to say, Akali Dal-BJP is an inseparable, deeply bonded relationship," he said.Six years later, a very different PunjabThe old partners are back again, but the state the BJP and SAD are returning to is markedly different from the one they left behind in 2020.The 2027 assembly election will be the alliance's first major state-level electoral test without Parkash Singh Badal, the five-time CM who died in April 2023. A towering figure in the Akali Dal, he was also a key bridge between the SAD and the BJP. Though Sukhbir Badal was already leading the party before his father's death, he now has to rebuild the party's standing without his political stature and influence.Another factor the alliance must keep in mind is that the farm issue has not disappeared. The repeal of the three farm laws did not automatically undo the distrust they created. Farmers' demands, including a legal guarantee for minimum support price, remain unresolved, keeping the issue politically alive in an agrarian state like Punjab. The BJP-SAD alliance will have to reckon with that trust deficit, particularly in the rural Malwa belt, which is the largest and most populous region covering major farming districts like Bathinda, Mansa, Sangrur, Patiala, Ludhiana and Muktsar.This is why the choice of Gurpurab for the reunion announcement is rich in symbolism. PM Modi had announced the repeal of the farm laws on the occasion in November 2021. The two parties have now chosen the same religious occasion to announce their political reconciliation. Whether that symbolism can translate into renewed trust among farmers is a different question.Another thing that has changed is that the Akali Dal can no longer assume that it commands the entire Panthic vote. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, independent candidates Amritpal Singh and Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa won from Khadoor Sahib and Faridkot, respectively. Between them, they also led in 15 assembly segments.ALSO READ: 'O Captain, My Captain' - Should Congress make room for Amarinder Singh again?This makes the party's return to its traditional Panthic space more difficult. The SAD has tried to reconnect with its core constituency through issues of Sikh identity and historical memory. The controversy surrounding 'Satluj', a film based on activist Jaswant Singh Khalra's work documenting alleged extrajudicial killings in Punjab, offered one such opportunity. After the film was taken down from an OTT platform, Sukhbir Badal announced screenings across the state, saying young people should know about the events it depicts.The bigger, bolder BJPSix years on its own have transformed the BJP from a junior partner that contested just 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats into a more assertive player. Under the old arrangement, the SAD contested 94 assembly seats and the BJP 23, largely in urban constituencies. For the Lok Sabha elections, the split was 10 seats for the Akalis and three for the BJP.Its vote share in the 2024 Lok Sabha election rose to 18.56 per cent, up from 9.63 per cent in 2019. The BJP contested all 13 seats in 2024, compared with just three under the old seat-sharing arrangement in 2019. Though it won no seats, the saffron party's vote share was higher than the SAD's 13.42 per cent. In the 2022 assembly election, the BJP had polled 6.60 per cent and won two seats.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The party has also strengthened its ranks through a steady stream of defections. In April 2026, AAP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha led six other MPs into the BJP which included Sandeep Pathak, Ashok Mittal, Harbhajan Singh, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Rajinder Gupta and Swati Maliwal. Six of these seven were Rajya Sabha members from Punjab. The exits dealt a major blow to the AAP's parliamentary strength and brought into the BJP leaders who had been closely associated with the party's Punjab strategy. Chadha and Pathak, in particular, had played key roles in the AAP's political and electoral planning.The BJP has since moved to put these former AAP leaders to work against their old party. Chadha and Harbhajan Singh have been named to its Punjab manifesto committee, while Pathak, Mittal, Sahney and other former AAP MPs have been assigned roles in the party's chargesheet committee, which will prepare its case against the Bhagwant Mann government.Earlier, in March 2024, AAP's then Jalandhar MP Sushil Kumar Rinku and Jalandhar West MLA Sheetal Angural had also joined the BJP. In November 2026, three more AAP legislators, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, crossed over. The BJP has also inducted senior Akali leaders, including Surinder Singh Chauhan and Jaswinderpal Sohal, as well as AAP functionaries from Moga led by spokesperson Navdeep Singh Sangha.The BJP's recruitment drive has not been limited to the AAP and SAD. Its Punjab ranks also include former Congress leaders such as Sunil Jakhar, Manpreet Singh Badal, Ravneet Singh Bittu and Preneet Kaur.That changes the terms of the reunion. The BJP returns with a larger vote share, a wider organisational footprint and experienced leaders. The SAD, meanwhile, needs the alliance to recover lost ground and reconnect with rural voters. Amit Shah has announced that the BJP is okay with the junior-partner label in the alliance. It is, however, unlikely that the BJP will settle for the old seat-sharing formula.Can the alliance unsettle AAP?The immediate target of the alliance is the AAP government, which swept to power in 2022 with 92 seats and 42.01 per cent of the vote. Its vote share fell to 26.02 per cent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when it won three seats, but it remains a formidable player.The SAD-BJP reunion gives the opposition a potentially stronger combination of urban and rural networks. It could also help consolidate voters who want an alternative to the AAP government. The drug problem, in particular, is likely to be a central campaign issue.At his press conference, Amit Shah listed three priorities for a future NDA government: eliminating drugs, eliminating corruption and strengthening nationalist forces. He promised that Punjab would be "completely drug-free" by December 31, 2029. He also targeted Congress, recalling Rahul Gandhi's 2017 promise that drugs would be eliminated within one term and accusing the party of doing nothing when it was in power.The attack gives the alliance a ready-made campaign plank. But it also puts the BJP and SAD on the spot, as both parties have been part of Punjab's political establishment for decades. The voters, thus, will judge their record as well as their promises.There is another complication. The Congress remains a strong third front and could split the anti-incumbency vote. Rural Sikh voters who continue to view the BJP through the lens of the farm agitation may also be reluctant to back the reunited partners. The AAP could benefit if opposition votes remain divided.The BJP-SAD reunion also complicates the Congress's position. With an established opposition pole, the contest for voters dissatisfied with the AAP government will now intensify. Amit Shah's attack on the Congress over its record on drugs made it clear that the alliance intends to take on both the ruling party and its principal rival.The Congress can still draw on its independent support base, but it will have to navigate a more crowded opposition space, as well as its own internal factional differences.Six years after a split that left both allies on the margins, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal have chosen pragmatism over past grievances to challenge AAP and Congress. The 2027 election, however, will not be a simple replay of the coalition's past victories. And tough seat-sharing talks are yet to be held.The OGs may be back together, but winning over a changed Punjab will require more than old chemistry.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A California couple lived together for nearly 10 years before marrying and later separating; a court has upheld the woman's right to half the pension benefits her partner earned during the years before their wedding
articles.summary: A California woman who lived with her partner for nearly 10 years before they got married has won the right to half of the pension benefits he built up
articles.body: A California woman who lived with her partner for nearly 10 years before they got married has won the right to half of the pension benefits he built up during those years. An appeals court turned down his effort to keep that money out of their property split. The California Court of Appeal backed a lower court's ruling that recognized Lisa Seiwald's ownership share in the pension earned by her ex-husband, Nicholas Irias, while they lived together from 1993 to 2003.The decision means Seiwald can claim half of the pension payments made by Irias and his employer during those years, plus the benefits that grew from them. The court said the couple had agreed to pool their pay and work and share whatever property they gained together, even before they wed. In its ruling in Seiwald v. Irias, the First Appellate District, Division Five, held that a California law shielding public pensions from debt collectors did not stop Seiwald from claiming her share. The court filed its decision on 28 September 2026 and updated it on 16 October, when it also turned down Irias's request for a new hearing without changing the result.Couple lived together before getting marriedAccording to the court judgment, Irias started working for the East Bay Municipal Utility District (EBMUD) in 1987, and both he and his employer paid into his pension during his career there, which lasted until 2018. Irias and Seiwald started dating in 1992 and moved in together the next year, staying together for almost 10 years before marrying in February 2003. In December 1993, the couple signed a domestic partnership form that let Seiwald get medical and dental coverage through Irias's job, and they also bought a house together in San Francisco in 1994.Even though they were not legally married for most of the time they lived together, Seiwald later argued they had agreed to treat their pay and property as jointly owned. She said the deal started when they moved in together in May 1993 and stayed in place until their wedding in February 2003. The fight later became part of their split, raising questions about whether pension benefits earned before marriage could count as shared property.Woman argued they had agreed to share earningsSeiwald filed for legal separation in September 2020 and later filed a separate civil lawsuit against Irias, claiming he broke their agreement over property gained during their relationship. According to the judgment, she said they had made a spoken agreement to combine their skills, efforts, labor, and pay and equally share the property built up from that work. California law recognizes such deals as Marvin agreements, named after the 1976 California Supreme Court case Marvin v. Marvin.Seiwald argued that their agreement covered Irias's pension payments as well as other property gained while they lived together, claiming he later refused to recognize her stake in his retirement benefits and blocked her from getting the share she believed was hers. The trial court looked at this dispute separately from the rest of their divorce case, holding a five-day trial to review the agreement and the property rights tied to it. It finally found that the couple had an unspoken agreement to pool their work and pay and split equally any property gained from those efforts, deciding that both people had a right to an equal share of the property covered by the deal.Husband challenged pension claimIrias fought the ruling, arguing his ex-partner could not claim part of his pension because the money was shielded under California's Public Utilities Code. He pointed to Section 12337, which generally makes public pension funds and payments impossible to transfer and protects them from seizure or other legal claims, a law meant to guard retirement funds from debt collectors and stop pension holders from losing their money in financial fights. Irias claimed that letting Seiwald take half of the pension earned before their marriage would wrongly create a loophole in those protections, and he rejected the idea that an unmarried partner could claim ownership of pension benefits under a deal made while living together.Seiwald pushed back against his argument, insisting she was not seeking the money as a debt collector, but was claiming an ownership right created by their agreement. She also argued that, even if the pension plan could not send the money straight to her, the court could order Irias to pay her an equal amount using other assets or money adjustments. The trial court agreed with her, ruling that she had a right to half of the pension benefits built up during the years covered by their deal, and said Irias could be ordered to pay her 50 percent of the relevant pension benefits once he started collecting them, or the court could use an expert calculation to value her share and order payment through other assets.Appeals court explains why pension protection did not applyIrias took the case to the California Court of Appeal, which agreed to look at one main legal question: whether Section 12337 stopped Seiwald from getting a share of the pension built up while they were unmarried. The appeals court did not revisit the lower court's finding that a Marvin agreement existed, instead accepting that finding in order to decide the pension question. In its review, the court drew a line between someone chasing pension money as a debt collector and someone who already holds an ownership stake in the property, explaining that pension shields generally stop debt collectors from seizing money belonging to a pension holder and do not wipe out ownership rights that another person gained through a valid property deal.The judges pointed to past California rulings, including Phillipson v. Board of Administration and In re Marriage of Brown, which held that pension payments earned on the job during marriage can be shared marital property, and also looked at the 1976 Marvin v. Marvin decision, which found that unmarried couples can make deals to pool their pay and share property gained while together. It said California law lets unmarried partners set up their finances through such deals, as long as they are not based on illegal terms. In Seiwald's case, the trial court had found that both partners agreed to pool their skills, labor, and pay and share the property built up from that work, which the appeals judges read as an agreement to treat property gained during the relationship just like shared property gained during a marriage, meaning Seiwald was claiming an ownership right she already had rather than trying to collect a debt from Irias.Court confirms equal share of pension contributionsThe appeals court decided that the pension payments made by Irias and EBMUD during the years covered by the agreement were part of the couple's shared property, including the benefits that grew from those payments. The judges turned down Irias's claim that the lower court had wrongly made his pension transferable to an unmarried partner, saying the ruling did not hand pension funds over to an outsider in the way Section 12337 forbids, and instead recognized Seiwald's ownership stake in property built up under their agreement.The court also cited Crossan v. Crossan, a past case where an ex-spouse was allowed to get other shared property equal in value to a stake in a retirement fund, seeing no reason why a similar fix could not work in this case if a direct payout from the pension was not allowed. The judgment stated that Seiwald had a right to an equal share of Irias's pension, including his own payments, the payments made by his employer, and the benefits earned from both during the years covered by their deal, and therefore upheld the trial court's order.Ruling does not settle every divorce issueThe appeals court's ruling dealt only with whether the pension shield law stopped Seiwald from claiming her share of the benefits earned before marriage, and it did not settle the rest of the money and property issues tied to the couple's split. The case will therefore go back to the lower court to handle the other matters connected to their divorce.The judgment also does not name an exact dollar amount that Irias must pay Seiwald right away, as the lower court had noted that her share could be figured out through the pension checks he receives or an expert valuation, with payment possibly made through other assets. The California Court of Appeal filed its first opinion on 28 September 2026 and issued an update to the opinion on 16 October while denying Irias's request for a new hearing, leaving the ruling unchanged in the case of Lisa Seiwald v. Nicholas Irias, heard by the First Appellate District, Division Five.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Iran live updates: 3 tankers attacked in Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
articles.summary: The IRGC Navy claimed Tuesday that several tankers hit naval mines.
articles.body:
Talks between the U.S. and Iran remain stalled despite the two countries signing a memorandum of understanding in June, aimed at ending the war that began with joint American-Israeli strikes on the country in February. The opening strikes killed a host of top Iranian officials and commanders, among them Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The two sides have continued to exchange strikes, though have not returned to the intense fighting seen in the early stages of the conflict. The U.S. says it is enforcing a naval blockade of the country's Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ports, while Iran claims control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz and continues to claim attacks on shipping transiting the waterway.

Meanwhile, intensified fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has seen the latter repeatedly attack Saudi military, oil infrastructure and transport facilities.

A tower in the financial district of the Saudi capital Riyadh was targeted in a "terrorist attack," a Saudi military spokesman said Tuesday. "One of the towers of the financial center was targeted in a cowardly terrorist attack," Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki, the spokesman for Saudi-led coalition forces fighting the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, posted on X. The post did not provide details about the nature of the attack. One of the towers in the Riyadh financial center was damaged last week when it was hit by a projectile. -ABC News' Othon Leyva

The United Kingdom Maritime Operations (UKMTO) Centre on Tuesday issued a warning after it received a report of three vessels being struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday evening. The vessels were reported to have continued their transit with all crew members accounted for, UKMTO said. Separately, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy on Tuesday claimed that several tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, the Islamic Republic News Agency reported. The IRGC Navy said the vessels were traveling through the strait "illegally." The IRGC has repeatedly claimed vessels have been damaged by naval mines, but U.S. Central Command has called previous claims false. -ABC News' Othon Leyva

Army chief Maj. Gen. Amir Hatami said on Tuesday that any resumption of U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iranian infrastructure would be met with "unimaginable" retaliatory infrastructure attacks. "We have now developed new operational plans to implement these new strategies and have made the necessary preparations," Hatami said, as quoted by the semi-official Mehr News Agency. "Should our infrastructure be struck again, we will strike their infrastructure in a way that is not easily reversible," he added.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Centre on Tuesday confirmed that a bulk carrier was hit by an "unknown projectile" while at anchor off the coast of the United Arab Emirates on Sunday. The incident occurred 23 nautical miles northeast of the Emirati east coast city of Khor Fakkan, the UKMTO alert said. "A fire was reported onboard the vessel but no casualties have been reported at this time," the alert said.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Monday that the proposed U.S. land blockade of his country "is impossible, both because of the country's vastness and the large number of provinces." U.S. Central Command announced earlier this month the formation of Task Force Iron Gate, which would be assigned "to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials." In comments published by the IRIB state broadcaster on Tuesday, Araghchi said Iran's "extensive connections with neighboring provinces in neighboring countries, high traffic and people-to-people ties, and historical and cultural roots on both sides of the border," meant that the U.S. task force would fail. "There are capacities in the country's provinces, especially the border provinces, that can open what the enemy wants to close to us," he added. "The duty of the country and the people is to discourage the enemies from imposing sanctions; the best way to counter these pressures is to discourage the sanctions takers from achieving their goals so that they know that this tool is not and will not be effective," Araghchi said. "Of course, this does not mean abandoning the other duty of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which is to open diplomatic channels for negotiations and lifting sanctions, and that path is also ongoing," he continued. -ABC News' Desiree Adib

President Donald Trump said in a social media post on Sunday night that "Iran has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year." "Don't worry, they've all been knocked down, and done no damage," Trump said of the Iranian attacks. Reported attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz have been higher in number in October and November than any previous months since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began in late February, according to data compiled by maritime organizations and analyzed by ABC News. Iranian forces have also been launching fresh missile and drone attacks on regional nations like Kuwait and Bahrain. -ABC News' Isabella Murray

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said at a Monday press conference that safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz can be restored quickly if the U.S. agrees to Iranian conditions for a full peace deal. "We are serious about fulfilling our commitments, upholding our rights and maintaining the conditions we have set," Baqaei said, as quoted by the state-run IRNA News Agency. "If the American side fulfills its commitments, security can be restored to the Strait of Hormuz and the region in the shortest possible time," he added.

"This does not mean overlooking the complexities surrounding the issue; rather, it simply underscores that the Islamic Republic of Iran knows what it wants, understands the rights of the Iranian people and their full scope, and will under no circumstances back down on this matter," Baqaei said. Baqaei said that Iran's conditions include the removal of what he called "cruel and unlawful sanctions," the lifting of the ongoing U.S. naval blockade and all other terms set out in June's memorandum of understanding.

U.K. Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) says they have received a report of an incident "involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman." Authorities are aware of the incident and investigations are ongoing, the UKMTO said. Separately, the IRGC navy, per official Iranian state media, say two tankers have "exploded and stopped due to collision with sea mines north of Ghanem Island and east of the Strait of Hormuz." The IRGC navy claims the tankers were passing through "unauthorized routes" and did not comply with instructions. It is not confirmed whether these two incidents are the same. -ABC News' Jamie Dorrington

Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Qatar issued statements on Sunday condemning Iran's attack on Bahrain on Saturday, which Manama said injured two people and caused a fire at a civilian industrial facility. Qatar's Foreign Ministry said the attack constituted a "flagrant violation of its sovereignty and territorial integrity, and a blatant breach of international law, the United Nations Charter, and the principles of good neighborliness." The Saudi Foreign Ministry described the attack as "heinous" and said it holds Iran responsible for the consequences of its continued perpetration of these flagrant attacks." Kuwait's Foreign Ministry said that Iranian attacks on Bahrain "threaten the region's security and stability."

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Sunday claimed to have shot down a U.S. MQ-1 Predator drone east of the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC made its claim in a statement carried by the state-run IRNA News Agency. U.S. Central Command did not immediately comment on the IRGC claim.

articles.title: Guru Nanak Jayanti, Kartik Purnima celebrated with devotion, fervour
articles.summary: Guru Nanak Jayanti and Kartik Purnima were celebrated in Ranchi and Jamshedpur with prayers, nagar kirtan, langar, Gatka displays and holy dips.
articles.body: Ranchi/Jamshedpur: The Sikh community in Ranchi, Jamshedpur and the rest of the state celebrated Guru Nanak Dev’s 557th birth anniversary with prayers, nagar kirtan and langar on Tuesday.At Guru Nanak Higher Secondary School in Ranchi, a special diwan was organised. Devotees offered prayers before Guru Granth Sahib, listened to shabad kirtan and recalled Guru Nanak Dev’s teachings on equality, honest living, compassion and service to humanity. The campus was decorated and langar was served.Governor Santosh Gangwar, Union minister of state for defence Sanjay Seth, Ranchi mayor Roshni Khalkho and MLA CP Singh visited the campus and paid obeisance. Gangwar said the Guru’s teachings remained relevant and urged people to follow his path. Seth said he envisioned a fatty liver-free India and Ranchi and called for healthier lifestyles.“Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s message is about serving humanity, treating everyone equally and spreading love,” said devotee Navin Singh Gurpal.In Jamshedpur, a 7.5-km nagar kirtan began from Sonari Gurdwara at 11.15 am after ardaas and concluded at Sakchi Gurdwara at 5.30 pm. Led by the Panj Pyare, the procession featured a decorated Palki Sahib carrying Guru Granth Sahib Ji. The 18-ft-high Palki Sahib was a major attraction.Six Gatka groups showcased Sikh martial art, while dastar-tying groups, religious organisations, social groups and schoolchildren participated. The procession passed through Kalgalnagar Road, River Meet Road and Jusco roundabout. Heavy vehicles were prohibited in the city from 5 am to 11 pm.CGPC president Bhagwan Singh said adopting Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s message of love, brotherhood, equality and service to humanity in everyday life would be the true tribute to the Guru.Meanwhile, devotees gathered at Subarnarekha river ghat in Chutia, Kanke and Dhurwa dams to mark Kartik Purnima, took holy dips, offered arghya to the rising sun, prayed and donated food and essentials before visiting temples.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: District-level epilepsy initiative wins international award
articles.summary: Project Ullas, an epilepsy care initiative from Gumla and East Singhbhum, wins Tadokoro Award at 16th AOEC; EpiCare app boosts rural follow-up.
articles.body: Gumla: Project Ullas, an epilepsy-care initiative rooted in Gumla and implemented in East Singhbhum, won the Tadokoro Award for clinical research at the 16th Asian and Oceanian Epilepsy Congress in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.Researcher Mayank Sharma, associated with the project in both districts, received the award on Monday. IAS officer Karn Satyarthi conceptualised the initiative during his tenures as deputy commissioner of Gumla and East Singhbhum, involving experts from AIIMS-New Delhi.Under the guidance of AIIMS neurology professor Dr Mamta Bhushan Singh, Sharma developed EpiCare, an open-source web application that enables frontline health workers to track seizures, medicine adherence and follow-ups.The East Singhbhum study covered 1,213 epilepsy patients, 91% of them from rural areas. Nearly two-thirds had either never taken anti-seizure medicines or had discontinued treatment before enrolment. The project recorded 9,016 follow-ups, with 99.3% of patients receiving at least one clinical contact.“The findings highlight the potential of technology-supported primary care to bring epilepsy follow-up closer to communities,” Sharma said.Satyarthi said the project treated epilepsy as a public health problem rather than merely a clinical issue. Project Ullas was also shortlisted for Prime Minister’s Award for Excellence in Public Administration 2025, he added.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.
